holidays.name: April Fools' Day
holidays.description: The world's most gleefully deceptive day, when people pull pranks, spread hoaxes, and shout 'April Fool!' at anyone gullible enough to believe that their shoe is untied or that the office is out of coffee forever.
holidays.origin: Nobody knows for sure. One popular theory ties it to France's 1500s switch from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar, which moved New Year's from April 1 to January 1. People who forgot or refused to change were mocked as 'April fools.' Others link it to ancient festivals like Hilaria or Chaucer's 1392 Canterbury Tales mention.
holidays.funFact: In 1957 the BBC aired a segment showing Swiss farmers harvesting spaghetti from trees. Hundreds of viewers phoned in asking how to grow their own spaghetti bush.

holidays.name: National Sourdough Bread Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the tangy, chewy, bubbly loaf that turned millions of home bakers into obsessive caretakers of jars of flour-and-water goo that they name like pets.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday cheered on by bakers and bread lovers, and popularized on social media after the sourdough baking boom. Sourdough itself dates back thousands of years, possibly to ancient Egypt.
holidays.funFact: Some sourdough starters are passed down for over 100 years, and San Francisco's famous sourdough gets its tang from a bacterium named Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis.

holidays.name: International Fun at Work Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to injecting joy, silliness, and laughter into the workplace, whether through office games, goofy hats, or a surprise pizza party, because spreadsheets are better with whoopee cushions.
holidays.origin: Created as an unofficial observance encouraging employers and employees to lighten up and boost morale. It conveniently lands on April Fools' Day, which makes the shenanigans nearly inevitable.
holidays.funFact: Studies on workplace happiness have repeatedly found that employees who have fun at work tend to be more productive and are less likely to quit.

holidays.name: Sorry Charlie Day
holidays.description: A day for gently pointing out that you are not Charlie the Tuna, the cartoon mascot who was perpetually rejected by Starkist because the company wanted tuna with good taste, not tuna with good taste in everything.
holidays.origin: Inspired by the advertising catchphrase 'Sorry, Charlie' from the long-running StarKist tuna commercials that debuted in 1961 and made rejection a household punchline.
holidays.funFact: Charlie the Tuna was voiced for many years by actor Herschel Bernardi, and his failure to ever get caught made him one of advertising's most lovable losers.

holidays.name: Fun Fact: National One Cent Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble penny, that copper-colored coin that lives in couch cushions, car cup holders, and 'take a penny, leave a penny' trays everywhere.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance celebrating the lowly one-cent coin, which has been minted in the United States since 1793 and has featured Abraham Lincoln since 1909.
holidays.funFact: It costs the U.S. Mint more than one cent to make a single penny, so every penny you find is technically worth less than the metal and labor that went into it.
